title: Practice 4: One direction, or round and about

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Did you go anywhere on Thanksgiving Day?
exercises.why: **ездил** is the past tense (masculine) of **ездить** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **ехать** for one direction. past: он е́здил · она е́здила · оно е́здило · они е́здили. — Wiktionary, «ездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  A past tense with no single goal in sight: repeated trips, or one completed round trip.  Compare: «В прошлом году я ездил в Россию.» (I went to Russia (and returned) last year.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Да, я ходил (ездил) туда утром.» (Yes, I went there in the morning.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  The other choice: **ехал** is from **ехать**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Ellie walked the rainswept streets home.
exercises.why: **шла** is the past tense (feminine) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. past: он шёл · она шла́ · оно шло́ · они шли́. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb идти means "to go, be going". It refers to going on foot. This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …).» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  «домой» gives a direction or a moment: one way, in progress, so the one-direction verb.  Compare: «Капитан идёт в штаб.» · «Он часто ходит в штаб.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Мы идём в библиотеку.» (We are headed to the library.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **ходила** is from **ходить**, the many-directions verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: My uncle has a business trip to Aomori tomorrow.
exercises.why: **едет** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **ехать** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ездить** for many directions. present: я е́ду · ты е́дешь · он е́дет · мы е́дем · вы е́дете · они е́дут. — Wiktionary, «ехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb ехать refers to going by some means of transportation, i.e. riding, driving: Я еду на поезде. (Я иду пешком.) Я еду в Европу. (Я иду в комнату.) This verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  «Note. — The present tense of the verbs иду, еду, лечу may also refer to a non-repetitive future action: Завтра он идёт на лекцию. В субботу мы едем в Нью-Йорк, а оттуда летим в Европу.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  Compare: «Капитан едет в город.» · «Он редко ездит в город.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Сегодня вечером мы едем в город.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  The other choice: **ездит** is from **ездить**, the many-directions verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
